questions.question: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. This equation is an example of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Redox.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Redox reactions **include a **change in the oxidation state** of the substrate.
 
• **Loss of electrons** or a** rise in the oxidation state **are both examples of** oxidation.**
 
• **Gaining electrons **or** lowering the oxidation state **are both considered to be **reductions.**
 
• In the reaction, CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, **Cu is reduced** whereas **Hydrogen is oxidized.**
 
• Redox reactions fall into one of **two categories:**
 
• **Electron-transfer:**
 
 
• Only one electron (typically) moves from the **reducing agent to the oxidant **during an electron transfer.
 
• It is common to talk about this kind of redox reaction in terms of** redox couples and electrode potentials.**
 
 
 
• **Atom transfer:**
 
 
• A transfer of an atom occurs when **one substrate gives way to another.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• A molecule, atom, or ion undergoes oxidation when it** loses electrons **as a result of a process.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition:**
 
 
• The process of **recycling nutrients** that have been **consumed by an organism** (plant or animal) to create its body begins with decomposition.
 
 
 
• **Reduction:**
 
 
• Reduction is the term used to **describe a reaction** in which a **reactant picks up electrons.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true/false?

Statements:

A. The following is an example of a reversible reaction

N2(g) + 3H2(g) rightleftharpoons 2NH3(g)

B. An example of the following photodecomposition reaction

CaCO3(s) xrightarrow{heat} CaO(s) + CO2(g)

options.text: Both A and B are true
Both A and B are false

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Irreversible chemical reactions** can occur in only one direction.

 
 
• The reactants can change to the products, but the products cannot change back to the reactants.
 
 
 
• **Reversible chemical reactions can occur in both directions. **
 
 
• The reactants can change to the products, and the products can also change back to the reactants.​​
 
• **Example** 
 
 
• N2(g) + 3H2(g) rightleftharpoons 2NH3(g)
 
• **Hence statement A is true.**
 
 
 
 
 
• ​CaCO3(s) xrightarrow{heat} CaO(s) + CO2(g)
 
 
• It is a **thermal** **decomposition reaction as Calcium carbonate undergoes decomposition and the carbon dioxide gas formed.**
 
 
• The second product of the reaction, the calcium oxide.
 
• The chemical reaction in which two or more products are formed from a single reactant is called** the ''Decomposition reaction”.**
 
• Photodissociation, photolysis, or photodecomposition is a chemical reaction in which a chemical compound is broken down by photons. 
 
 
 
• **Hence statement B is not true.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• A combination reaction is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: X + Y → XY.
 
• The combination of two or more elements to form one compound is called a combination reaction.
 
• Other types of Chemical Reactions:
 
 
• Decomposition reaction: The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones.
 
 
• AB → A + B.
 
 
 
• Precipitation reaction: Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming.
 
 
• A + Soluble salt B → Precipitate + soluble salt C.
 
 
 
• Neutralization reaction: An acid and a base react with each other. Generally, the product of this reaction is salt and water.
 
 
• Acid + Base → Salt + Water.
 
 
 
• Combustion reaction: Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic, meaning they give off heat. 
 
 
• A + O2 → H2O + CO2.
 
 
 
• Displacement reaction: One element takes place with another element in the compound. 
 
 
• A + BC → AC + B.

questions.question: How many moles are present in 60 g Helium of ?
questions.solution:
• Number of grams of Helium (He) = 60 gm
 
• Molecular mass is the sum of total protons and neutrons.
 
• The molecular mass of Helium = 2 × 2 = 4
 
• Now multiply the mass with a number of elements we get = 4 × 1 = 4
 
• One mole is equal to the total mass of the molecule.
 
• We know one mole is equal to 4 gm of Helium molecule.
 
• Now a number of moles in 60 gm of Helium is (n) = 60/4

n = 15 moles

 
• The number of moles in 60 gm is 15 moles.

questions.question: What is liberated when copper are heated with concentrated H₂SO₄?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SO₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When copper is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4), copper sulfate, sulfur dioxide (SO2), and water are formed.
 
• The balanced chemical reaction is:** Cu + 2H2SO4 → CuSO₄ + SO2 + 2H₂O**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Copper, being a transition metal, participates in a variety of chemical reactions. Here are some significant ones:
 
 
• Cu(NO3)2 (s) → CuO (s) + NO2 (g) + O2 (g)
 
• CuSO4 (s) → CuO (s) + SO3 (g) + O2 (g)
 
• Cu (s) + 2H2SO4 (conc) → CuSO4 (aq) + SO2 (g) + 2H2O (l)
 
• 2Cu (s) + O2 (g) → 2CuO (s)

questions.question: 25°C is equivalent to how many degrees on the Fahrenheit scale?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __77__ °__Fahrenheit.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Celsius is used in most of the world to calculate temperatures. At 0° Celsius, water freezes and boils at 100 °Celsius.
 
• Fahrenheit is a scale widely used in the United States for calculating temperatures.
 
• °Fahrenheit = {(9/5) x °Celsius} + 32 
 
• °Fahrenheit = (9/5) x 25 + 32
 
• °Fahrenheit = 45 + 32
 
• °Fahrenheit = 77°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• 80 °Fahrenheit = 26.67 °C
 
• 75 °Fahrenheit = 23.89 °C
 
• 87 °Fahrenheit = 30.56 °C

questions.question: Which gas is emitted by the reaction of chloroform and HNO3 ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloropicrin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between **chloroform (CHCl₃)** and **nitric acid (HNO₃)** produces **chloropicrin (CCl₃NO₂)**.
 
• **Chloropicrin** is also known as **PS**, and it has been used as a **chemical warfare agent** and a **soil fumigant**.
 
• The reaction is an example of **halogenation and oxidation**, where chloroform is both halogenated and oxidized by nitric acid.
 
• **Chloropicrin** acts as a **tear gas** and can cause severe eye and respiratory irritation, along with nausea and vomiting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 
 
 

 1) Tear Gas
 Tear gases are chemical compounds that irritate the eyes, causing a burning sensation, pain, and tears. Chloropicrin can act as one.
 
 

 2) Methyl isocyanate
 A highly toxic and volatile chemical used in the production of pesticides. Not produced by chloroform and HNO₃ reaction.
 
 

 3) Chloropicrin
 Produced by the reaction of chloroform with nitric acid, used historically as a chemical weapon and currently as a soil fumigant.
 
 

 4) Lewisite
 A chemical warfare agent that blisters the skin and mucous membranes. Not related to chloroform and HNO₃ reaction.

questions.question:
Acid + Metal → Salt + ________

Which of the following is needed to complete the reaction above?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen gas.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• When an **acid reacts with a metal, salt and hydrogen gas are formed.**
 
• The reaction between an acid and a metal has the following **general word equation:**

Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen.

 
• In the above reaction, **metal displaces hydrogen atoms from acids as hydrogen gas, resulting in the formation of salt.**
 
• For example:**Mg + 2HCl = MgCl2 + H2**

​Magnesium + hydrochloric acid = magnesium chloride + hydrogen gas

 
• In the above reaction, **Metal (Zn) displaces hydrogen atoms from the acid (NaOH) as hydrogen gas (H2) and forms a compound called sodium zincate salt **(Na2ZnO2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**Hydrogen gas is not formed** when a** metal reacts with dilute nitric** **acid **because **nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent.**

questions.question: Mass of 0.1 mol of glucose will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 g**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Explanation:

__
 
• 0.1 mole of C₆H₁₂O₆ = Molecular mass of C6H12O6 in grams

 
 
• 0.1 (Mass of 6C + Mass of 12H + Mass of 6O)
 
• 0.1 (12 × 6 + 1 × 12 + 16 × 6)
 
• 0.1 (72 + 12 + 96)
 
• **18 grams**__

questions.question:
To which category of reactions does the following chemical reaction belong? 

NaCl₍ₐq₎ + AgNO₃₍ₐq₎ → NaNO₃₍ₐq₎ + AgCl₍ₛ₎
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Double displacement reaction.__**

**__Concept__:**

**Chemical reaction:**

__
 
• It is a process in which one or more substances, the reactants, are converted to one or more different substances, the products.
 
• A chemical reaction rearranges the constituent atoms of the reactants to create different substances as products.

**Explanation__:**

__
 
• 
 
Double displacement reaction: 

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which two compounds react and exchange their ions forming new products. 
 
• This reaction often results in the formation of an insoluble compound called a precipitate. 
 
• Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A⁺B⁻ + C⁺D⁻ → A⁺D⁻ + B⁻C⁺

**​In the given chemical reaction: **

NaCl(aq) + AgNO3(aq) → NaNO3(aq) + AgCl(s)

The reactants NaCl and AgNO₃ have exchanged their ions to form** NaNO3 and AgCl. **

**Thus, it is an example of a double displacement reaction.**__​

**__Additioⁿal Iⁿformatioⁿ__**

__Types of Chemical Reactions:__

Combination reaction:

 
• Two or more elements or compounds combine together to form a single compound.
 
• Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + B → AB.

Decomposition reaction:

 
• The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones.
 
• Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: AB → A + B.

Displacement reaction:

 
• One element takes place with another element in the compound.
 
• Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + BC → AC + B.

**Redox reaction:**

 
• It is a reaction in which one species is reduced and the other is oxidized. 
 
• Reduction means losing Oxygen or gaining hydrogen 
 
• Oxidation means gaining oxygen or losing hydrogen.
